newsitem.title: DUBAI: GCC chief urges Iran to end row over Gulf islands.
newsitem.headline: GCC chief urges Iran to end row over Gulf islands.

text.p: The head of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) has urged Iran to respond to peace initiatives to resolve a dispute with council member United Arab Emirates (UAE) over three Gulf islands.

"It is in the interest of Iran to accept such proposals as its gains from boosting GCC confidence outweigh those of its occupation (of the islands)," said GCC Secretary-General Jameel Hujilan in comments published on Saturday by UAE's al-Ittihad daily.

The UAE has urged Iran to agree to take the row over the islands of Greater Tunb, Lesser Tunb and Abu Musa to the International Court of Justice. Iran says its sovereignty over the islands is not negotiable but has called for bilateral talks with the UAE to clear up any "misunderstandings".
The two sides held talks in Abu Dhabi in 1992 but these did not resolve the dispute.
The GCC, which groups Saudi Arabia, Oman, Qatar, Bahrain Kuwait and the UAE, terms the Iranian presence on the islands "occupation" and deplores Iranian "measures to consolidate" it.
The six Gulf oil states said Iran was trying to establish the status quo by force over the three islands near key oil shipping lanes.

UAE Foreign Minister Rashid Abdullah al-Nuaimi said in an address to the U.N. General Assembly earlier this month that Iran had built an electrical plant on Greater Tunb and an airport, refrigeration plant and fishing plant on Abu Musa, while Iranian nationals, mostly from the military, had been settled on the islands.
